Title: Define and apply the two CMA Agents
Description: mariella-consultant and mariella-client created as versioned Agent configs in the T&G Anthropic org; engine mounted per session rather than pasted as a system prompt.

Title: Orchestrator session driver
Description: orchestrator/run-session.mjs mounts engine + tenant files, drives one session per tenant (answers ask_user_input and free-text prompts), harvests /mnt/session/outputs into a pluggable store.

Title: S3 per-tenant durable store
Description: One T&G-owned bucket, per-tenant prefix tenant/<id>/project/, versioning on, all public access blocked; S3Store behind the same interface as localStore, selected by MARIELLA_STORE.

Title: Folder-preserving harvest (W67)
Description: CMA file transfer carries a filename and never a folder, so the folder is encoded into the filename (every / becomes ~) and decoded on harvest. Verified both directions including a 2-deep path.

Title: Correct the sandbox mount paths
Description: CMA honours mount_path but re-roots it under /mnt/session/uploads; bootstraps now name the real effective paths so the agent stops hunting for the engine on every run.

Title: Publish the agent updates (v8/v9) and re-sync the lock
Description: Batch the bootstrap + model changes into a single in-place update per agent; re-sync deploy/agents.lock.json to the returned version. Never recreate an agent.

Title: Close the consultant-to-client handover
Description: Transport is proven; the handoff is not. The client engine gates its reference read on 01-client-knowledge/marketing-strategy-confirmed.md, which only exists after a consultant pass completes the audit and confirm-strategy stages. Needs one full consultant run.

Title: Per-tenant concurrency lock
Description: run-session.mjs has no lock, against the architecture's one-session-per-tenant contract. Latent on one laptop, real the moment two people share a host.

Title: Deploy the orchestrator to an always-on host
Description: Provision the EC2 host with an SSM + scoped-S3 IAM role, service user, Node 20, ant CLI, read-only deploy key; today the orchestrator runs from a laptop.

Title: Choose the server auth model for ant
Description: The real decision in the deploy plan: how the service user authenticates to Anthropic on an unattended box, and what the credential renewal story is.

Title: First real run and operating procedure on the server
Description: Smoke-test a throwaway tenant on the local store, then a real S3 run against the proven tenant, confirm write-back, and write down the two operating limitations.

Title: Extract session-core from the CLI
Description: Pull the create/stream/answer/harvest loop into orchestrator/lib/session-core.mjs with injected getInput/onEvent so the CLI and the web server share one path. CLI behaviour must be byte-identical.

Title: Archive sessions after successful harvest
Description: Closes the sessions-accumulate operating limitation. Archive sessions only; never agents or environments.

Title: Tenant registry
Description: Which agent version, which vaults, which durable-store prefix per tenant.

Title: Prove tenant isolation with a test
Description: Isolation is largely Anthropic-enforced; verify with a real test rather than assuming. One tenant's session must not see another's files or vault.

Title: Per-tenant Vaults for client credentials
Description: Client credential substituted into outbound calls at egress and never entering the agent. Designed, not built.

Title: Wire GA4, Search Console and LinkedIn as MCP servers
Description: Until integrations are wired, audits run on public-web inference only — half information. Every credentialed integration goes through MCP/Vaults so no token reaches a prompt or tool argument.

Title: Decide per-integration credential wiring
Description: MCP-wrapped OAuth (Anthropic auto-refreshes; best for LinkedIn/Google) versus an environment-variable credential substituted at egress (simplest for static keys). Validate per integration.

Title: Verify OAuth auto-refresh
Description: Confirm Vault refresh works so the in-prompt LinkedIn token-expiry check can be retired.

Title: Click-to-connect onboarding flow
Description: OAuth connect for LinkedIn/Google, paste-key for the rest, written straight into the tenant's Vault. Guided connection is step one of onboarding.

Title: Enforce the onboarding integration gate
Description: Setup does not run until GA4 + Search Console + LinkedIn are connected and live in the tenant Vault. A degraded run is flagged and held, never shipped clean.

Title: Confirm no secret reaches T&G-side storage
Description: Prove nothing sensitive lands in a T&G database, log or the durable store.

Title: Probe the three CMA unknowns before promising UI
Description: Gate on the web front: whether mid-session file input is accepted, whether a session can be re-attached after the stream closes mid-ask_user_input, and whether files.list can be polled mid-session.

Title: Extract the brand tokens for app surfaces
Description: brand/tokens.css (colours, type scale, radii, shadows) de-bundled from the landing page; workspace chrome ported from the audit-report template family, not the bundler blob.

Title: Web server with per-tenant auth
Description: Cloudflare Access JWT verified against the team's public keys, email mapped to tenants and role, 403 for anything unmapped. Server binds localhost only; the tunnel is the sole ingress.

Title: Session, upload and outputs endpoints
Description: start/stream/answer/done with a lock check and an idle timeout that auto-harvests; upload endpoint with size cap, type allowlist and sanitised ~-encoded filenames; outputs served from a sandboxed viewer hostname with CSP sandbox and nosniff.

Title: Per-tenant human access log
Description: Append-only tenant/<id>/access-log.jsonl covering login-seen, session start/end, uploads and file views — the connection-ledger precedent applied to people.

Title: Dashboard-first client UI
Description: Login lands on the outputs view (latest audit, monthly report, outcome join table), newest first, with a real empty state. Session panel renders ask_user_input options as buttons, upload control describes its actual behaviour honestly, mobile-usable.

Title: Operator-only surfaces
Description: Role-gated layer picker (consultant/client), tenant switcher across granted tenants, raw session trace. Clients see none of it.

Title: Cloudflare tunnel, hostnames and Access policies
Description: cloudflared as a systemd service (outbound only), two hostnames (app + sandboxed file viewer), one Access application each with a per-tenant email allowlist and block-by-default. Needs the domain and Cloudflare account admin.

Title: Two-tenant silo verification
Description: Two throwaway tenants, two browsers, two emails: A cannot list, fetch, see or start a session as B, including direct URL attempts. Same-tenant second tab refused by the lock. Planted script tag confirms the viewer sandbox holds.

Title: Rehearse the Taryn demo path (W52)
Description: Login as a client, dashboard with Wink-shaped outputs, one short session interaction, upload, report refresh. Rehearsed before the regroup.

Title: Ops units and deploy runbook
Description: systemd units for the web app and cloudflared with Restart=always and journald; API key fetched from Secrets Manager at start, never written to disk. Deploy is git pull plus restart — documented, not automated.

Title: Decide client interface scope
Description: Full custom UI versus a thinner approvals surface. Shapes the largest phase; Cowork used to provide this surface.

Title: Add the join table to the audit template
Description: A per-asset table (content asset, channel, conversion type, outcome, join_basis) as section 1 of the audit, ahead of the qualitative narrative. Requires deciding the repeating-row mechanism, since the template has no loop construct.

Title: Add the CONVERSION_OUTCOMES capability
Description: HubSpot as the only provider; the join key is EDM click recipient email to HubSpot contact to associated deals; HubSpot form identity discriminates client-enquiry from talent-application. No provider means the capability is unavailable, not silently degraded to engagement metrics.

Title: Rework the audit scope and the refusal path
Description: No CRM connection is a refusal, not a downgrade: the audit still covers site, SEO and competitive position but will not report engagement metrics as performance findings. Includes an anti-restatement rule against presenting metrics the client can already read natively.

Title: Client-side monthly report parity
Description: Apply the same join-first treatment to the client engine's visual report stage, kept in engines/stages/ and fetched on demand so the per-turn size cut holds.

Title: Verify the refusal actually fires
Description: Run a consultant pass with no CRM connected: if it produces a conventional audit anyway, the instruction lost to the surrounding 4,000 lines and placement must be strengthened. Then a run with a CRM to confirm the join table renders.

Title: Re-run the placeholder parity check and re-upload the engines
Description: Assemble both engines, re-run the 99/99 template-to-engine placeholder parity check, upload to the Files API (immutable, mints new IDs), update both engine_file_ids and bump both agent versions in the lock and the YAML specs.

Title: Verify skill-fetch pinning
Description: The skill CDN reference must be a pinned ref, not a moving branch. Flagged as an open risk; confirm whether it was ever completed.

Title: Reconcile drift between the two engine layers
Description: build/drift-report.md exists; the reconciliation has not been done.

Title: Decide engine delivery hardening
Description: Whether to split into a lean sub-100K core system prompt plus stage playbooks as on-demand CMA skills, replacing the mounted-file approach.

Title: Cadence via CMA scheduled deployments
Description: Convert the weekly/monthly cadence to cron-fired sessions that start autonomously; retire the in-prompt token-expiry check once Vault refresh covers it.

Title: Export session capability records to the warehouse
Description: Tenant-tagged export of the engine's normalised DATA SOURCE RESOLUTION records, which are already tool-agnostic and source-tagged.

Title: Ingestion exclusion filters
Description: Provably drop excluded record types at ingestion: no secrets, no CRM/audience/email records, no named individuals. Company-level only.

Title: k-anonymity query layer
Description: Minimum cohort N of 5 to 10 with small-cell suppression for benchmark reports; re-identification is the top risk given a niche B2B client base.

Title: Benchmark priors as an engine input
Description: Feed cross-client benchmarks back into PLAN. Must be true first: 3 to 5 clients live.

Title: CMA running-cost view (W45)
Description: No cost view exists; the model was chosen on feel. This blocks the pricing decision and everything downstream of it.

Title: Per-run metering to usage.jsonl
Description: After harvest, append tenant, layer, session id, tokens, estimated cost and timestamp to tenant/<id>/usage.jsonl in S3 — real numbers to feed the pricing work.

Title: Finalise pricing
Description: Subscription, 13-month contract at the 12-month price, API cost bundled to a credit allowance, overage invoiced next month with a 90% alert and no hard stop. Escalated as critical; blocked on the cost view.

Title: Reconcile EC2 framing to CMA across all collateral
Description: Nearly every pricing and meeting artefact still says EC2 or server hosting; that framing was superseded on 22 Jul. Reconcile everywhere pricing touches.

Title: Sales collateral actions
Description: Resend the sales folder, post the recording with sensitive parts stripped, write user docs, produce a demo video.

Title: Effort tuning on mechanical sessions
Description: Drive cost per turn down by lowering reasoning effort on mechanical stages. Also revisit the model choice — the revert to Opus 4.8 at xhigh is materially more expensive per run and was flagged as worth reconsidering before cadence runs.

Title: Engineer prompt caching
Description: Named as load-bearing for the margin case; the ~75-80% figure depends on it.

Title: Eval harness
Description: Nothing currently scores output quality.

Title: Eval dashboard v1 to the beta
Description: A screen-shareable view of eval results for the beta client.

Title: Per-stage model field
Description: A declared model per stage as a swap seam, so a model change is configuration rather than a rewrite. Moves portability off Locked.

Title: Pre-pilot security review
Description: Confirm every credentialed integration goes through MCP/Vaults with no token in any tool argument; review prompt and log surfaces.

Title: DPA, benchmark opt-in and deletion path
Description: Anthropic listed as a sub-processor; B2B commercial opt-in at onboarding plus an MSA data-use clause; a deletion and withdrawal path.

Title: Monitoring, alerting and store backup/restore
Description: Instance status alarm, plus a tested backup and restore path for the durable store.

Title: Self-hosted-sandbox escape-hatch drill
Description: Prove the flip of one tenant's execution to T&G-owned infrastructure, so the escape hatch is real before a client needs it. Must be true first: the server is stable.

Title: Migrate one pilot client off client-hosted onto the platform
Description: The pilot gate: one client running entirely on the hosted platform.

Title: Ship the server and onboard client #2
Description: Hypothesis: runs stay isolated under real multi-tenancy. Kill line: not live by month 3, stop.

Title: Land the first paying client at the quoted price
Description: Hypothesis: the ICP pays this price. Kill line: no one pays by month 3, reprice. There are no paying clients yet.

Title: Close the deal-outcome join
Description: Hypothesis: campaign IDs resolve to deals. Kill line: under 50% resolution by week 12, drop attribution.

Title: Cut human oversight to two hours or less per client
Description: Hypothesis: golden rows shrink the review queue. Kill line: over 4 hours at month 3, reprice as a service. Oversight is the swing factor in the margin.

Title: Publishing autonomy
Description: Let the engine publish without a human in the loop, without losing sender-of-record. Must be true first: over 99% on the action.

Title: Outcome-based pricing pilot
Description: Meter attributed enquiries instead of a flat subscription. Must be true first: attribution is trustworthy.

Title: Instrument first-pass acceptance and rework rate
Description: Measure the share of assets accepted without edit, per client. M4 sets the target at 70% with a kill criterion below it across two clients; M1 sets rework above 30% on two consecutive clients as a reprice trigger. Nothing currently measures either, so neither kill criterion can fire.
Source: 04-the-contract/golden-dataset.md; 01-the-bet/prototype.md (decided in M1/M4, absent from the export)

Title: Per-channel restyling in the engine
Description: The Shadow AI audit found operators pasting finished assets into a chatbot to restyle them per channel — recurring, and decided as build rather than partner. Hand-restyling is oversight time, so this feeds the oversight target.
Source: 05-the-guardrails/compounding-system.md (decided in M5, absent from the export)

Title: Quote $2,500 to 3-5 ICP prospects
Description: Put the price in front of real buyers ahead of a signature. Hypothesis: the ICP will pay this price. Kill line: zero verbal yes by month 3, reprice. The leading indicator for MAR-65.

Title: Five ICP discovery calls
Description: Talk to five AU lean marketing teams in the $200K-$1M spend band about the job they would hire for. Tests whether the displaced-hire framing is the one they recognise.

Title: HubSpot Breeze counter-position
Description: Write the answer to the named competitive risk: what Mariella does that a suite AI attached to their existing CRM does not. The AI eval calls the USP not-landing and nothing in the build backlog addresses it.

Title: Turn the Wink beta into a reference case
Description: Get the delivered Wink audit on the record as a named reference. Hypothesis: a named reference converts prospects. Kill line: the beta will not go on record, find another reference.
